s7.title: Behind the Bumpers | 2046 Bear Metal | Side Climber | Charged Up Robot

bet.text: Climb the charge station from its side: partners only need to balance two robots while this one runs another cycle or two.

demand.text: For scoring, the team put a very light arm first: it has to reach all three levels without tipping the robot.

cycle.text: The arm collects inside the frame perimeter. It then extends while the robot drives into the community, so the robot can score at once; the elbow does most of the moving.

endgame.text: An automated sequence: two paws come down and push the robot up until the front wheel gets over, belts raise its angle along the charge station, then the arm tips back onto hard stops to level it and it keeps climbing. Climbing the side does not affect the tilt.

gave_up.text: The belts under the chassis were the hardest part of the climb. If it breaks, the team cannot really replace it, but it presumed the climb would be pretty reliable.

changed.text: The interview is from the Bonney Lake event, which the interviewer calls the team's second; the championship version is not described.

By its second event this was the third intake on the arm and about the seventh prototype; the claw had been designed and made in about a week. The team was considering separate motors for the two sides of the belt drive, instead of linked sides.

outcome.text: 61-21-2 in official play; ranked 9 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 75.88, Hopper).

solves.text: Give the ground clearance the side climb needs

facts.text: Chosen over SDS swerve for ground clearance and compact size

solves.text: Fit bumpers quickly and make room outside the frame for the climb gearboxes

facts.text: Brackets with a standoff slide into a hole in the chassis and toggles snap down to hold them
3D-printed inserts at the swerve modules space the bumpers from the chassis, leaving room outside for the climb gearboxes

solves.text: Get onto the charge station from its side so partners need only a two-robot balance

facts.text: Two independent paws, each on one NEO with a gear reduction and chain
Belts run in 2x2 tubes under the chassis, driven by a 775 motor through a VersaPlanetary to 3D-printed pulleys

cost.text: The belt drive was the hardest part and cannot really be replaced if it breaks, though the team presumed it would be pretty reliable
